scope_notes: Approximately four-hour hands-on Pandas microcourse with six tutorial/exercise pairs covering data creation/loading, indexing, summary functions, grouping/sorting, dtypes/missing values and combining/renaming data.
required_resources: Modern browser and free Kaggle account for notebooks/exercises and certificate; no paid compute required for the course

component_evidence.pedagogy: Every lesson pairs concise explanation with executable notebook work, keeping the course centered on doing rather than watching.
component_evidence.depth: Six focused lessons provide a strong practical introduction but cannot replace a broader data-analysis curriculum.
component_evidence.practice: Short hands-on challenges are the core of the course and require direct manipulation of DataFrames throughout.
component_evidence.materials: Tutorials and hosted executable exercises are integrated in the Kaggle environment with no local setup.
component_evidence.currency: The course is live and issuing certificates in 2026; core Pandas operations remain current, though library details should be monitored over time.
component_evidence.expertise: Kaggle Learn is built by data-science educators and practitioners around real notebook workflows.
component_evidence.accessibility: No-cost browser notebooks, no local setup and a free certificate make the route exceptionally accessible.

recommendation_rationale: Excellent practical Pandas onboarding with almost no setup friction. It is highly recommendable as a focused skills module, not as a standalone data-science foundation.

scope_notes: Approximately four-hour visualization course with eight lesson/exercise stages covering Seaborn, line/bar/heatmap/scatter/distribution plots, chart selection/style, a final project and creating independent notebooks.
prerequisites: Basic Python familiarity is helpful; Pandas knowledge improves transfer
required_resources: Modern browser and free Kaggle account; hosted notebooks remove local-library setup

component_evidence.pedagogy: The route progresses from individual chart types to chart selection, styling and a final applied project.
component_evidence.depth: It teaches a useful visualization workflow but remains a short library-centered course rather than a full data-visualization curriculum.
component_evidence.practice: Each lesson includes executable exercises and the course culminates in a final project.
component_evidence.materials: Hosted notebooks, examples and exercises are coherent and setup-free.
component_evidence.currency: The course is live in 2026, but its Seaborn-centered API examples are more version-sensitive than timeless visualization principles.
component_evidence.expertise: Kaggle Learn provides practitioner-oriented data-science instruction and realistic notebook workflows.
component_evidence.accessibility: No-cost hosted notebooks and certificate make practical visualization accessible without local setup.

recommendation_rationale: A strong practice-first visualization microcourse with a real final project. Library/API dependence creates more currency risk than the underlying design principles.

scope_notes: Approximately three-hour introductory SQL course with six tutorial/exercise pairs covering BigQuery workflow, SELECT/FROM/WHERE, GROUP BY/HAVING/COUNT, ORDER BY, aliases/CTEs and joins.
prerequisites: No advanced database prerequisite; basic data familiarity is helpful
required_resources: Modern browser and free Kaggle account; exercises use hosted BigQuery-backed notebooks without learner-paid infrastructure

component_evidence.pedagogy: The lessons introduce SQL syntax in a practical query workflow and immediately require learners to execute queries on hosted data.
component_evidence.depth: Six lessons cover the essential beginner query toolkit but do not reach database design, transactions or administration.
component_evidence.practice: Every topic has a corresponding executable exercise, producing strong learning density for a three-hour route.
component_evidence.materials: Hosted tutorials and query exercises remove setup and database-provisioning friction.
component_evidence.currency: Core SQL is stable and the current BigQuery workflow remains live in 2026; vendor-specific details create only a modest transferability risk.
component_evidence.expertise: Kaggle Learn instructors teach SQL in a realistic data-analysis context.
component_evidence.accessibility: Free hosted infrastructure, short duration and certificate create extremely low access friction.

recommendation_rationale: An excellent first SQL practice route for data analysis. Its compact scope and BigQuery framing mean it should complement rather than replace a fuller database course.

scope_notes: Approximately four-hour follow-on SQL course with four tutorial/exercise pairs covering JOIN/UNION patterns, analytic/window functions, nested/repeated BigQuery data and efficient query writing.
prerequisites: Kaggle Intro to SQL or equivalent SQL fundamentals
required_resources: Modern browser and free Kaggle account; hosted BigQuery-backed exercises

component_evidence.pedagogy: A focused progression takes learners from relational combination into analytical SQL and BigQuery-specific complex-data patterns.
component_evidence.depth: The course adds meaningful advanced querying skills but remains only four lessons and is partly BigQuery-specific.
component_evidence.practice: All lessons include executable query exercises using hosted data.
component_evidence.materials: The tutorial/exercise pairing is coherent and requires no learner-managed database setup.
component_evidence.currency: Window functions and query-efficiency concepts are durable; nested/repeated data and tooling examples introduce BigQuery specificity.
component_evidence.expertise: Kaggle Learn provides practical SQL/data-platform expertise oriented toward analytical workflows.
component_evidence.accessibility: The course is free and hosted, though it assumes prior SQL knowledge and is less universal because of BigQuery-specific material.

recommendation_rationale: A dense and useful analytics-SQL follow-on, especially for BigQuery users. Its narrow four-lesson scope prevents it from ranking like a comprehensive database pathway.

scope_notes: Approximately four-hour intermediate tabular-ML course covering missing values, categorical variables, preprocessing pipelines, cross-validation, XGBoost and data leakage through tutorial/exercise pairs.
prerequisites: Kaggle Intro to Machine Learning and Pandas or equivalent Python/tabular-ML familiarity
required_resources: Modern browser and free Kaggle account; hosted notebooks provide the practical environment

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course is organized around common failure modes and workflow improvements that immediately matter in real tabular ML projects.
component_evidence.depth: Seven focused lessons add meaningful intermediate workflow competence but remain narrow compared with full machine-learning courses.
component_evidence.practice: Every lesson includes executable notebook exercises, reinforcing preprocessing, validation and model-building decisions.
component_evidence.materials: Hosted notebooks and clean tutorial/exercise pairs keep the practical route coherent and setup-free.
component_evidence.currency: Pipelines, cross-validation, leakage and categorical handling remain current; the specific XGBoost/tabular stack still needs periodic currency checks in fast-moving ML.
component_evidence.expertise: Kaggle Learn is strongly aligned to practical data-science competition and notebook workflows.
component_evidence.accessibility: The course is free and browser-native, though prerequisite knowledge is real.

recommendation_rationale: One of the highest-return short ML workflow courses for learners who already know the basics. It is a specialist skills accelerator, not a general ML foundation.
